calls.head: The Hurricanes should drive the play
calls.body: The Hurricanes have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Blackhawks one of the worst. Expect the Hurricanes to spend more of the night in the Blackhawks’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

calls.body: The Hurricanes shoot from anywhere, and the Blackhawks are near the bottom of the league at stopping it. Spencer Knight had better be ready from the opening faceoff.

CAR.head: We gave Carolina a 76% chance, and they delivered.

surprises.head: Chicago hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Chicago is one of the league’s lightest-hitting teams. Even by those standards, this was a quiet night on the body: a hit score of 27 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 76 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

story.head: The Hurricanes beat the Blackhawks
paras: Mark Jankowski struck first for the Hurricanes late in the first. It was a busy second period. Sebastian Aho stretched the lead to 2-0 shorthanded early in the period, and Jackson Blake made it 3-0 a little over a minute later. Roman Kantserov, in his sixth NHL game, scored his first NHL goal a little over a minute later to get the Blackhawks on the board. Taylor Hall stretched the lead to 4-1 a minute and a half later, and Jordan Martinook made it 5-1 early in the third. Oliver Moore made a dent in Carolina’s lead with less than six minutes left, bringing it to 5-2.

The Hurricanes carried the play, outshooting the Blackhawks 39-26, and got the result to match. Brandon Bussi made 24 saves for the Canes, and Spencer Knight allowed five goals on 39 shots. The Hurricanes improved to 4-1-1 and climbed into first in the Metropolitan, while the Blackhawks dropped to 1-5-0, still last in the Central.

items.text: Four straight wins for the Hurricanes.
Sebastian Aho has a point in five straight games.
Jordan Martinook scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 2 (ten games played since).
Andrei Svechnikov’s point streak ended at four games.
